R code for: Miller, E. J., Steward, B. A., Witkower, Z., Sutherland, C. A. M., Krumhuber, E. G., & Dawel, A. (2023). AI hyper-realism: Why AI faces are perceived as More real than human ones. *Psychological Science.*
Contact details: amy.dawel@anu.edu.au

The analyses herein are for Miller et al. (2023) Experiment 2 - attributes.

# Load R packages

Here, we load the required R packages.

```{r, setup, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE}

#clear workspace
rm(list = ls())

#list packages 
lib <- (c("rmarkdown", #RStudio markdown
          "knitr", #generating RStudio output
          "readr", #read in data
          "kableExtra", #extra tools for styling kable tables in R markdown knit
          "tidyverse", #also loads ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, readr, purrr, tibble
          "Hmisc", #miscellaneous          
          "psych", #core psychology functions e.g. ANOVA
          "psycho", #for signal detection analyses
          "apaTables", #for APA table output
          "lme4", #linear modelling
          "sjPlot", #for tab_model
          "rstatix", #for checking outliers
          "ggpubr", #for publishable plots
          "ggpmisc", #stat_fit_glance function
          "rlist" #for saving lists
          ))

#load packages
for (i in 1:length(lib)){
  pkg <- lib[i]
library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
}

#turn off scientific notation
options(scipen = 999)

#set date for file saving
dt <- Sys.Date()

```

# Load & organise datasets

Here, we load the datasets for male and female participants separately.

Variable labels are generally formatted as follows:

-   Letter 1 = real or synthetic (r or s)

-   Letter 2 = black or east asian or south asian or white (b or e or s or w)

-   Letter 3 = male or female (m or f) Number = stimulus number from 1-50

-   Suffix codes are:
.attr = How attractive is this face?
.ligh = How congruent are the lighting and shadows across this picture?
.expr = How emotionally expressive is this face?
.fami = How familiar is this face?
.qual = How good is the quality of this picture?
.happ = How happy is this person genuinely feeling?
.memo = How memorable is this face?
.dist = How much would this face stand out in a crowd?
.agyr = How old is this person?
.prop = How proportional is this face?
.smoo = How smooth is this person's skin?
.symm = How symmetrical is this face?
.eycn = Is this person making eye contact with you?
.aliv = When you look at this person's eyes, how alive do they seem?

```{r, load-data}

#import raw data separately from male and female participants
df.malePs <- read.csv("../data/LM_Expt2attributes_malePs.csv", na.strings = "")
df.malePs <- as.data.frame(df.malePs)
df.malePs$ProlificGender <- "Male"
df.femalePs <- read.csv("../data/LM_Expt2attributes_femalePs.csv", na.strings = "")
df.femalePs <- as.data.frame(df.femalePs)
df.femalePs$ProlificGender <- "Female"

```

Here, we bind the male and female participant data together and set-up the data for further analyses.

```{r, data-wrangling}

#bind female and male data together 
df.allPs <- rbind(df.femalePs, df.malePs)

#remove cases that never started study
df.allPs <- filter(df.allPs, !is.na(prolificId))

#remove superfluous variables
df.allPs <- select(df.allPs, -contains(c("firstclick", "lastclick", "clickcount", "prac1", "prac2", "submit")))

#convert to tibble
df.allPs <- as_tibble(df.allPs)
df.allPs$AIaware <- "no"

#cleanup: remove dfs that are no longer needed
rm(df.malePs, df.femalePs)

```

# Data corrections

Here, we correct responses where participants messaged via Prolific that they had made a mistake or experienced problems with the experiment. The chunk provides each participant message in full and if/how their data was managed.

```{r, data-corrections}

#ResponseId: R_1dGgmM8JDFxmB7H
#Prolific message = "Hello, on the last question i selected the wrong option, I meant to select rating how smooth the face appeared. Sorry about this."
#attentionCheck recoded as "How smooth is this person's skin?"
df.allPs$attentionCheck[df.allPs$ResponseId == "R_1dGgmM8JDFxmB7H"] <- "How smooth is this person's skin?"
```

# Data screening

Here, we compute each participant's missing data for each of the face types.

NB. We did not analyse RTs because the experiment was administered using Qualtrics on participants own hardware and therefore factors other than participant performance may have contributed to RTs (e.g., internet speed).

```{r, missing-data}

#compute missing data
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  #compute N ratings missing for each face type
    mutate(rwm.rating.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".rating"))))) %>%
    mutate(swm.rating.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".rating"))))) %>%
    mutate(rwf.rating.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".rating"))))) %>%
    mutate(swf.rating.miss = rowSums(is.na(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".rating"))))) %>%
    mutate(rw.rating.miss = 50 - rwm.rating.miss - rwf.rating.miss) %>%
    mutate(sw.rating.miss = 50 - swm.rating.miss - swf.rating.miss)

#code which face sex each participant saw
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>% 
  mutate(face.sex.cond = case_when(rwm.rating.miss == 50 ~ "female faces",
                                   rwf.rating.miss == 50 ~ "male faces"))
  
```

Here, we compute accuracy for the catch trials.

```{r, compute-catch}

#recode data for catch trials as correct or incorrect, according to the value participants were asked to rate the item as
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>% 
  #male catch trials
  #bs edit: removed case when as specific requirement so can be used with ifelse(). Also separated to be vertical to be easier to read
  mutate(m.catch1.rating = ifelse(m.catch1.rating == 72,1,0)) %>% 
  mutate(m.catch2.rating = ifelse(m.catch2.rating == 43,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(m.catch3.rating = ifelse(m.catch3.rating == 20,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(m.catch4.rating = ifelse(m.catch4.rating == 67,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(m.catch5.rating = ifelse(m.catch5.rating == 88,1,0)) %>%
  #female catch trials 
  mutate(f.catch1.rating = ifelse(f.catch1.rating == 57,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(f.catch2.rating = ifelse(f.catch2.rating == 11,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(f.catch3.rating = ifelse(f.catch3.rating == 95,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(f.catch4.rating = ifelse(f.catch4.rating ==  8,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(f.catch5.rating = ifelse(f.catch5.rating == 36,1,0)) 

#sum correct catch trials
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%  
 rowwise() %>%
  mutate(catch.acc = rowSums(across(contains("catch")), na.rm = TRUE))

```

# Select included sample

Here, we screen the sample to select participants who meet inclusion/exclusion criteria and also code the reasons for participant exclusions.

```{r, data-included}

#identify cases to exclude
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
      mutate(exclude = case_when(
        Progress < 97 ~ "exclude", #exclude if <97% complete
        str_detect(operateSys, "Android") ~ "exclude", #exclude if used phone
        operateSys == "iPhone" ~ "exclude", #exclude if used phone
        confirmWhite != "Yes, my ethnicity is White/European/Caucasian" ~ "exclude", #exclude if not White
        USstate == "I do not reside in the United States" ~ "exclude", #exclude if not resident in US
        yearsOutsideUS > 2 ~ "exclude", #exclude if >2 years outside US prior to 18
        incNoCond != "No, none of these statements apply to me" ~ "exclude", #exclude if reported condition likely to affect face processing
        AIaware == "yes" ~ "exclude", #exclude if response indicated aware faces were AI
        catch.acc < 4 ~ "exclude", #exclude if more than 1 catch trial incorrect
        attentionCheck == "How attractive is this face?" & rating.cond != "attractiveness" ~ "exclude", #exclude if failed attention check
        attentionCheck == "How congruent are the lighting and shadows across this picture?" & rating.cond != "lighting and shadows" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How emotionally expressive is this face?" & rating.cond != "expressivity" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How familiar is this face?" & rating.cond != "familiarity" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How good is the quality of this picture?" & rating.cond != "image quality" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How happy is this person genuinely feeling?" & rating.cond != "happiness" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How memorable is this face?" & rating.cond != "memorability" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How much would this face stand out in a crowd?" & rating.cond != "distinctiveness" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How old is this person?" & rating.cond != "age" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How proportional is this face?" & rating.cond != "proportionality" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How smooth is this person's skin?" & rating.cond != "skin texture" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "How symmetrical is this face?" & rating.cond != "symmetry" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "Is this person making eye contact with you?" & rating.cond != "eye contact" ~ "exclude",
        attentionCheck == "When you look at this person's eyes, how alive do they seem?" & rating.cond != "aliveness" ~ "exclude",
        rw.rating.miss > 5 ~ "exclude", #exclude if >10% trials missing for any condition
        sw.rating.miss > 5 ~ "exclude"
        )) 

#code reasons for exclusions
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
    mutate(excReason.incomplete = case_when(
      Progress < 97 ~ "incomplete")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.phone = case_when(
      str_detect(operateSys, "Android") ~ "used phone", operateSys == "iPhone" ~ "used phone")) %>% 
    mutate(excReason.white = case_when(
      confirmWhite != "Yes, my ethnicity is White/European/Caucasian" ~ "not White")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.notUS = case_when(
      USstate == "I do not reside in the United States" ~ "not living in US")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.yrsOutUS = case_when(
      yearsOutsideUS > 2 ~ ">2 yrs outside US pre-18")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.condFP = case_when(
      incNoCond != "No, none of these statements apply to me" ~ "condition affecting face processing")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.AIaware = case_when(
      AIaware == "yes" ~ "AI aware")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.catch = case_when(
      catch.acc < 4 ~ ">1 error on catch trials")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.attCheck = case_when(
      attentionCheck == "How attractive is this face?" & rating.cond != "attractiveness" ~ "failed attention check", 
      attentionCheck == "How congruent are the lighting and shadows across this picture?" & rating.cond != "lighting and shadows" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How emotionally expressive is this face?" & rating.cond != "expressivity" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How familiar is this face?" & rating.cond != "familiarity" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How good is the quality of this picture?" & rating.cond != "image quality" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How happy is this person genuinely feeling?" & rating.cond != "happiness" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How memorable is this face?" & rating.cond != "memorability" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How much would this face stand out in a crowd?" & rating.cond != "distinctiveness" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How old is this person?" & rating.cond != "age" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How proportional is this face?" & rating.cond != "proportionality" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How smooth is this person's skin?" & rating.cond != "skin texture" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "How symmetrical is this face?" & rating.cond != "symmetry" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "Is this person making eye contact with you?" & rating.cond != "eye contact" ~ "failed attention check",
      attentionCheck == "When you look at this person's eyes, how alive do they seem?" & rating.cond != "aliveness" ~ "failed attention check")) %>%
    mutate(excReason.miss = case_when(
      rw.rating.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
      sw.rating.miss > 5 ~ ">10% missing in 1 or more conditions",
  )) 

#concatenate reasons for exclusions into a single variable
df.allPs <- df.allPs %>%
  mutate(excReason = paste(excReason.incomplete, excReason.phone, excReason.white, excReason.notUS, excReason.yrsOutUS, excReason.condFP, excReason.AIaware, excReason.catch, excReason.attCheck, excReason.miss, sep = "; ")) %>%
  mutate(excReason = gsub("NA; ", "", excReason)) %>%
  mutate(excReason = gsub("NA", "", excReason))

#generate dataset for included Ps
df.incPs <- df.allPs %>%
  filter(is.na(exclude))

#generate dataset for excluded Ps
df.excPs <- df.allPs %>%
  filter(exclude == "exclude") 

#save data
write.csv(df.incPs, paste("../data/LM_Expt2attributes_includedPs.csv"))
write.csv(df.excPs, paste("../data/LM_Expt2attributes_excludedPs.csv"))

#table showing Ns for male vs female Ps across conditions for included Ps
x <- table(df.incPs$rating.cond, df.incPs$face.sex.cond, df.incPs$gender)
sum(x)

#cleanup: remove dfs that are no longer needed
rm(df.excPs)

```

# Compute scores

Here, we compute scores for each of the face types.

```{r, compute-scores}

#compute mean ratings for each face type
df.incPs <- df.incPs %>%
  rowwise() %>%
    mutate(rwm.rating = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwm0") & ends_with(".rating")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(swm.rating = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swm0") & ends_with(".rating")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rwf.rating = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rwf0") & ends_with(".rating")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(swf.rating = rowMeans(across(starts_with("swf0") & ends_with(".rating")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rw.rating = rowMeans(across(starts_with("rw") & contains("0") & ends_with(".rating")), na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    mutate(sw.rating = rowMeans(across(starts_with("sw") & contains("0") & ends_with(".rating")), na.rm = TRUE))

#replace NaN's with NA's
df.incPs[df.incPs == "NaN"] <- NA

#save data
write.csv(df.incPs, paste("../data/LM_Expt2attributes_includedPs_scored.csv"))

```

# Descriptives

Here, we get key descriptives for our selected sample for each of the fourteen rating conditions.

```{r, describe, warning = FALSE}

#making rating condition factor
df.incPs$rating.cond <- as.factor(df.incPs$rating.cond)

#sample descriptives
descript.sampByCond <- df.incPs %>%
  dplyr::group_by(rating.cond, face.sex.cond) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    n = n(),
    nMan = sum(ProlificGender == "Male"), #Prolific rather than self-identified
    nWom = sum(ProlificGender == "Female"), 
    age.mean = mean(age),
    age.min = min(age),
    age.max = max(age),
    age.sd = sd(age)
  )
write.csv(descript.sampByCond, paste("../output/LM_Expt2attributes_descriptives_sampByCond.csv")) #save key sample descriptives

#stimulus descriptives
descript.stimByCond <- df.incPs %>%
  group_by(rating.cond) %>%
  group_map(~ describe(.x))
names(descript.stimByCond) <- levels(df.incPs$rating.cond) #names items in list by rating condition

#extract means from list
means.stimByCond <- lapply(descript.stimByCond,"[", 3) #where column 3 is means
means.stimByCond <- data.frame(matrix(unlist(means.stimByCond), nrow=length(descript.stimByCond), byrow=TRUE)) #convert to dataframe
means.stimByCond$rating.cond <- levels(df.incPs$rating.cond) #add variable for condition
naming <- colnames(df.incPs) #naming columns
naming <- naming[! naming %in% c("rating.cond")]
naming <- append(naming, "rating.cond")
colnames(means.stimByCond) <- naming

write.csv(means.stimByCond, paste("../output/LM_Expt2attributes_descriptives_stimByCond.csv")) #save full stimulus and sample descriptives

```

# Reshape wide data into long format

Here, we reshape our data into long format.

```{r, reshape-w2l}

#remove superflous variables
dfl.anova.part <- df.incPs %>%
  select('ResponseId', 'rating.cond', 'rwm.rating':'swf.rating') %>%
  select(-contains(c("catch"))) #%>%
  #select(-contains(c("rw"))) #use this option to remove real faces to analyse AI faces only
  #select(-contains(c("sw"))) #use this option to remove AI faces to analyse real faces only

#convert data required for ANOVA and t-tests to long format BY PARTICIPANT
dfl.anova.part <- df.incPs %>%  
  gather("FaceType", "mean.rating", c(rwm.rating, swm.rating, rwf.rating, swf.rating), convert = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(face.sex = substr(FaceType, 3, 3)) %>%
  mutate(face.format = substr(FaceType, 1, 1)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mean.rating))
dfl.anova.part$face.sex <- as.factor(dfl.anova.part$face.sex)
dfl.anova.part$face.format <- as.factor(dfl.anova.part$face.format)

#convert data required for ANOVA and t-tests to long format BY STIMULUS
dfl.anova.stim <- means.stimByCond %>%
  select('rating.cond', starts_with('swm0') | starts_with('rwm0') | starts_with('swf0') | starts_with('rwf0')) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(-rating.cond), names_to = "faceId") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(rating.cond)) %>%
  mutate(face.sex = substr(faceId, 3, 3)) %>%
  mutate(face.format = substr(faceId, 1, 1)) %>%
  gather("rating.cond", "mean.rating", age:symmetry, convert = TRUE)
dfl.anova.stim$face.sex <- as.factor(dfl.anova.stim$face.sex)
dfl.anova.stim$face.format <- as.factor(dfl.anova.stim$face.format)

#remove superflous variables
dfl.icc <- df.incPs %>%
  select('ResponseId', 'rating.cond', 'rwm001.rating':'swf009.rating') %>%
  select(-contains(c("catch"))) #%>%
  #select(-contains(c("rw"))) #use this option to remove real faces to analyse AI faces only
  #select(-contains(c("sw"))) #use this option to remove AI faces to analyse real faces only

#convert data required for ICCs to long format
dfl.icc <- df.incPs %>%  
  gather("FaceId", "rating", rwm001.rating:swf009.rating, convert = TRUE) %>%
  #gather("FaceId", "rating", swm001.rating:swf009.rating, convert = TRUE) %>% #to analyse AI faces only
  #gather("FaceId", "rating", rwm001.rating:rwf009.rating, convert = TRUE) %>% #to analyse real faces only
  filter(!is.na(rating))

```

```{r, participant-plots}
#add bars to indicate mean

#add violin geom to indicate distribution
rating.vplots <- rating.vplots + geom_violin(alpha = 0.4, aes(color = face.format))
#change colour manually: http://sape.inf.usi.ch/quick-reference/ggplot2/colour

  scale_color_manual(values=c("#5D3A9B", "#E66100"))
```

# Statistical analyses

```{r, statistical-analyses}

dfl.anova.part.splitConds <- split(dfl.anova.part, dfl.anova.part$rating.cond)
df.ttest.splitConds <- split(df.incPs, df.incPs$rating.cond)
dfl.icc.splitConds <- split(dfl.icc, dfl.icc$rating.cond)
splitNames <- c("df.age", 
              "df.aliveness", 
              "df.attractiveness", 
              "df.distinctiveness", 
              "df.expressivity", 
              "df.eye.contact", 
              "df.familiarity", 
              "df.happiness", 
              "df.image.quality", 
              "df.lighting.shadows", 
              "df.memorability", 
              "df.proportionality", 
              "df.skin.texture", 
              "df.symmetry")

aov.output <- NULL
aov.output <- as.data.frame(aov.output)
stats.output <- NULL
stats.output <- as.data.frame(stats.output)
reliability.output <- NULL
reliability.output <- as.data.frame(reliability.output)
for (i in 1:length(dfl.anova.part.splitConds)) {
    assign(splitNames[i], dfl.anova.part.splitConds[[i]])
    assign(splitNames[i], dfl.icc.splitConds[[i]])
    cond.name <- splitNames[i]
#ANOVA; here we produce an ANOVA with face.sex.cond between subjects and CG-human within subjects.
    aov.out <- anova_test(
      data = dfl.anova.part.splitConds[[i]], dv = mean.rating, wid = ResponseId,
      within = c(face.format), between = c(face.sex)
      )
    aov.out <- as.data.frame(aov.out)
    aov.out$cond <- splitNames[i]
    aov.output <- rbind(aov.output, aov.out)
#pairwise comparisons; here, we compare mean ratings for CG vs human for each of the rating conditions.
    rw.sw <- t.test(df.ttest.splitConds[[i]]$rw.rating, df.ttest.splitConds[[i]]$sw.rating, paired = TRUE) #male and female faces combined
    rw.sw.t <- rw.sw$statistic
    rw.sw.df <- rw.sw$parameter
    rw.sw.p <- rw.sw$p.value
    rwm.swm <- t.test(df.ttest.splitConds[[i]]$rwm.rating, df.ttest.splitConds[[i]]$swm.rating, paired = TRUE) #male faces only
    rwm.swm.t <- rwm.swm$statistic
    rwm.swm.df <- rwm.swm$parameter
    rwm.swm.p <- rwm.swm$p.value
    rwf.swf <- t.test(df.ttest.splitConds[[i]]$rwf.rating, df.ttest.splitConds[[i]]$swf.rating, paired = TRUE) #female faces only
    rwf.swf.t <- rwf.swf$statistic
    rwf.swf.df <- rwf.swf$parameter
    rwf.swf.p <- rwf.swf$p.value
#ICCs; here, we compute the observer (participant response) and stimulus (face) contributions to variance in the ratings, following code provided by Hehman, E., Sutherland, C. A., Flake, J. K., & Slepian, M. L. (2017). The unique contributions of perceiver and target characteristics in person perception. *Journal of personality and social psychology, 113*(4), 513.
    model <- lmer(rating ~ 1 + (1 | ResponseId) + (1 | FaceId), data = dfl.icc.splitConds[[i]])
    df.x <- assign(cond.name, as.data.frame(VarCorr(model))) #Will return, in part, a section labeled ‘random effects’.
    FaceId.est <- df.x[1, "vcov"]
    ResponseId.est <- df.x[2, "vcov"]
    Residual.est <- df.x[3, "vcov"]
    stimulus.icc <- FaceId.est / (FaceId.est + ResponseId.est + Residual.est) * 100
    observer.icc <- ResponseId.est / (FaceId.est + ResponseId.est + Residual.est) * 100
    residual.icc <- Residual.est / (FaceId.est + ResponseId.est + Residual.est) * 100
    check.icc <- stimulus.icc + observer.icc + residual.icc
    stats.output <- rbind(stats.output, data.frame(cond.name, rw.sw.t, rw.sw.df, rw.sw.p, rwm.swm.t, rwm.swm.df, rwm.swm.p, rwf.swf.t, rwf.swf.df, rwf.swf.p, FaceId.est, ResponseId.est, Residual.est, stimulus.icc, observer.icc, residual.icc, check.icc))
#The first two numbers in the summary represent the taus (τ) for rater and target, respectively. 
#The bottom value (labeled residual) is sigma squared (σ2) in the ICC equation in Hehman et al. (2017). 
#To calculate rater ICC.
#ICC = rater tau / (sigma squared + rater tau + target tau).
#To calculate target ICC.
#ICC = target tau / (sigma squared + rater tau + target tau).
#The resulting numbers represent the percentage of variance from between-rater (rater-ICC) or between- #target (target-ICC), respectively. 
#reliability: here we calculate Cronbach's alphas for each rating condition 
    df.y <- (df.ttest.splitConds[[i]])
    df.y <- select(df.y, ends_with(".rating"))
    df.y.male.ai <- select(df.y, contains(c("swm0")))
    alpha.male.ai <- alpha(df.y.male.ai)
    a.male.ai <- alpha.male.ai[["feldt"]][["alpha"]][[1]]
    lci.a.male.ai <- alpha.male.ai[["feldt"]][["lower.ci"]][[1]]
    uci.a.male.ai <- alpha.male.ai[["feldt"]][["upper.ci"]][[1]]
    df.y.female.ai <- select(df.y, contains(c("swf0")))
    alpha.female.ai <- alpha(df.y.female.ai)
    a.female.ai <- alpha.female.ai[["feldt"]][["alpha"]][[1]]
    lci.a.female.ai <- alpha.female.ai[["feldt"]][["lower.ci"]][[1]]
    uci.a.female.ai <- alpha.female.ai[["feldt"]][["upper.ci"]][[1]]
    df.y.male.hum <- select(df.y, contains(c("rwm0")))
    alpha.male.hum <- alpha(df.y.male.hum)
    a.male.hum <- alpha.male.hum[["feldt"]][["alpha"]][[1]]
    lci.a.male.hum <- alpha.male.hum[["feldt"]][["lower.ci"]][[1]]
    uci.a.male.hum <- alpha.male.hum[["feldt"]][["upper.ci"]][[1]]
    df.y.female.hum <- select(df.y, contains(c("rwf0")))
    alpha.female.hum <- alpha(df.y.female.hum)
    a.female.hum <- alpha.female.hum[["feldt"]][["alpha"]][[1]]
    lci.a.female.hum <- alpha.female.hum[["feldt"]][["lower.ci"]][[1]]
    uci.a.female.hum <- alpha.female.hum[["feldt"]][["upper.ci"]][[1]]
    reliability.output <- rbind(reliability.output, data.frame(cond.name, a.male.ai, lci.a.male.ai, uci.a.male.ai, a.female.ai, lci.a.female.ai, uci.a.female.ai, a.male.hum, lci.a.male.hum, uci.a.male.hum, a.female.hum, lci.a.female.hum, uci.a.female.hum))
}

write.csv(aov.output, paste("../output/LM_Expt2attributes_anovas_incPs.csv")) #save ANOVAs
write.csv(stats.output, paste("../output/LM_Expt2attributes_ttests_iccs_incPs.csv")) #save ttests & ICCs
write.csv(reliability.output, paste("../output/LM_Expt2attributes_reliability_incPs.csv")) #save Cronbach's alphas

```
